Ayahuasca Retreat in Bolivian Amazon Pisatahua
Skip to content
Ayahusca Retreat
Aquiquana Reserve, Bolivia
Pisatahua Ecolodge is a sacred space in the Bolivian Amazon to work with plant medicines, including ayahuasca.
Found in the heart of the Aquicuana Reserve, our 80-hectare center is situated in an area of impressive biodiversity.
This breathtaking location provides an ideal environment to heal, expand consciousness, and connect with the wonders of the Amazon.
Ayahuasca Retreats
Our healers  come from diverse backgrounds of wisdom-traditions from the Amazon and Andes.
They are responsible and respected community members, dedicated to the shamanic path, with decades of experience.
Alongside our support staff, we hold small-group retreats with honor,  safety  and respect.
Healers & Staff
Our healers  come from diverse backgrounds of wisdom-traditions from the Amazon and Andes.

Sean W
Trustindex verifies that the original source of the review is Google. Worth Your Time and Trust When trying to research retreats from afar, it can be incredibly difficult to figure out what the experience will really be like. The people that offer plant medicines-healers, shaman, etc-have radically different approaches and attitudes, and my number one priority was to find a safe, supportive, and compassionate retreat for my wife and I. After all, traveling to the rainforest to open up at a Dieta is a huge undertaking. An experienced, compassionate healer can make the experience transformative, while a disingenuous shaman can leave you struggling through a tough time. If you are lucky enough to have the chance for a retreat with Ximena and Natalia at Pisatahua, you should take it. Pisatahua is such a well thought out and put together experience. Long before you arrive Erik is available to answer all of your questions and ensure that you ready for the stay. His advice is invaluable to making the most of the retreat. The more you put into the retreat beforehand-by following the advice on diet, taking the time to write an honest bio, and thinking about your reasons for going-the better the experience can be. Taking part in a Pisatahua retreat supports something much larger than the continued offering of retreats. The massive reserve that the retreats take place in also supports local livelihoods through fishing and sustainable forest management, and it contains a research center that visiting scientists work from, supported by the nonprofit Kaypacha. We stayed in a private cabin overlooking the lake and enjoyed the sights and sounds of the rainforest from our hammock. Scientists at the Research Center took us on a guided walk through the rainforest, which gave names and stories to the creatures we saw and heard. Our retreat took place during the dry season which meant very few mosquitos -apart from dusk and dawn. We found the food to be delicious (the menu is determined by the healer). Fresh local fish, vegetables, fruits, and grains, always prepared carefully to ensure that everyone stays well. The fried Yucca was especially tasty! The water in the bathrooms and showers comes up clean from a deep well, and every room/space had purified drinking water available. As for Ximena and Natalia, I can’t say enough good things. Ximena’s ceremony is completely unique. Rather than keeping attendees passive and introverted, Ximena weaves in opportunities for participation in moments of ritual (and they are totally voluntary). She keeps a strong container, stays cool when things heat up, and always leads with compassion and wisdom. She and Natalia are always available for you, in and out of ceremony. They take the time to read your bio, and they really do help you heal. They offer practical practices and exercises that you can carry with you after the retreat. With so much thought, skill, and love at your back, you can take the leap and have a truly transformative, life-affirming experience in a rainforest reserve that you’re helping to support. I can’t wait to go back.

Pisatahua: Remote Jungle Retreat with First Class Accommodations
Skip to content
Accommodations
Comfort & Sustainability
Pisatahua was carefully designed to maximize the comfort of our guests, while minimizing our impact on the environment.  All cabins were constructed with sustainably harvested secondary-growth rainforest materials.  We went to great lengths to minimize the removal of any vegetation and utilize energy efficient technologies.   For more information on our sustainable living measures, please refer to our  Ecolodge Sustainability page.
Cabins
All cabins were designed through the adaptation of local construction techniques to meet the needs of our guests.  We worked hard to ensure they are comfortable, clean and safe.  Cabins are secluded from their neighbors and extremely spacious (30 square meters/ 323 square feet).  They are fully furnished with with running water, private bathrooms, washbasins and showers.  Cabins have extremely high-pitched roofs and sit one meter above the jungle floor.
Each cabin room comes equipped with 2 twin/or 1 super-king bed, shelving, low-watt lighting, candles, night-stands, an indoor hammock, a writing desk, chairs, and fresh drinking water. We also provide fresh linens, towels and can arrange for laundry service.
All cabins are situated facing the lake with enormous windows to maximize ventilation and views of the Aquicuana Reserve.
La Maloka
The Maloka is a large octagonal-shaped structure with a domed-shaped thatched roof made from palm leaves.  Its spacious layout is entirely open with a 360 degree panoramic view. The Maloka is the largest building and ceremonial center of the retreat center.  All ceremonies take place in the maloka and it also serves as a space for group-discussions, meditation, yoga and Tai Chi instruction.  The Maloka is connected via a raised path to our dock and cabin on the Aquicuana Lake.  Guests are always welcome to respectfully use this space however they choose.
The Maloka is equipped with mattresses, pillows, blankets, buckets, yoga mats and hand towels.  Additionally, there is a large altar with numerous items of spiritual power. Our public bathrooms are located 10 meters outside the maloka.  The bathrooms are connected via a raised walkway to allow for easy and safe access.

Amazon Ayahuasca Retreat | Boat from Riberalta, Bolivia
Skip to content
Location in Riberalta
Pisatahua’s Amazon Location
Pisatahua is an hour journey from the town  Riberalta .  The center operates on 80 hectares of private land within the Aquicuana Reserve.
Arriving to Riberalta, Bolivia
Plane : The airline Ecojet has daily flights to Riberalta with connections from nearly every major city in Bolivia.  The prices on the Ecojet website are not accurate Pisatahua can often help secure prices much cheaper than what you will find online.  Please contact us and we ll help organize your connecting flight to Riberalta together.
Bus: The journey by bus to Riberalta is an excellent way to explore the country and see areas where few travelers have been.  The trip costs about 200 Bs ($30 usd) from La Paz and takes about 18 hours; from Santa Cruz about 24 hours.  There are options to break up the journey and we can provide suggestions on interesting places to stay along the way.
* We meet guests in Riberalta and transport them to Pisatahua at no additional cost.  If you have any questions about planning your arrival, please don’t hesitate to contact us .
The Aquicuana Reserve:
The Aquicuana Reserve (Área Protegida y Reserva Natural Aquicuana) is located about 25 kilometers from the town of  Riberalta  in the Beni Department of Bolivia. Its name, ‘Aquicuana,’ comes from the Tacana native language, meaning “land of the giant trees.”
In addition to our retreat center, the Reserve is home to two communities (San Jose and Warnes) and the picturesque lake, ‘Lago Aquicuana.’  In 2016, Pisatahua and the local communities worked to expand and formalize the protection of areas surrounding the lake.  Together, the group established the Aquicuana Reserve, providing protection to more than 20,000 hectares of rainforest.
With the support of biology volunteers, Pisatahua’s been building an inventory of the plant and animal species to raise awareness locally and internationally of the need to protect this unique and diverse ecosystem.  We’ve been amazed at the biodiversity discovered.  Thus far we’ve identified more than  350 bird species  alone.

pages.text:
Frequently Asked Question (FAQs) on an Ayahuasca Retreat
Skip to content
FAQ s
Travel Questions:
How do I arrive?
Your final destination is  Riberalta, Bolivia.  When flying from another country, you’ll have to fly to either the  Santa Cruz (VVI)  or  La Paz (LPB) airport first, and then take a connecting flight to Riberalta. There are daily flights to Riberalta with the airline EcoJet ( http://ecojet.com.bo/ ) .
For International Travelers, we generally recommend guests fly into Santa Cruz and take a connecting flight with Ecojet.
Some struggle to make this purchase from abroad.  If you have any issues, we can purchase your ticket and then you can reimburse us later.
When should I arrive to Riberalta?
We ask all guests to arrive the day before the retreat begins. We can help reserve a hotel in Riberalta.
We can also arrange expeditions to explore Riberalta and the surrounding areas.
When do you leave for Pisatahua?
We typically leave for Pisatahua around 10:30 am. We will coordinate the exact time with each participant.
We pick up all guests at their hotel and transport them to the retreat center.  Transportation is included in retreat fees.
When should I book my return flight?
You are welcome to book your return flight (from Riberalta) the day the retreat is scheduled to end. Most guests choose take a flight the same day the retreat ends; however, guests are also welcome to extend their stay in Riberalta.
We will transport guests from Pisatahua to the airport, hotel, or bus station. We’ll coordinate with each guest to ensure they make their connecting flights or bus.
Will I be picked up at the airport?
If you arrive on the day the retreat begins, we will meet you at the airport and transport you to the retreat center. If you arrive days before the retreat starts, we will meet you at your hotel/hostal and transport you to the retreat center. A taxi from the airport to any hotel is maximum 20bs ($3usd). Transportation to and from Pisatahua is included in the retreat fees.
Can I arrive by bus?
The journey by bus can be a bit unpredictable, especially during the rainy season. Nevertheless the trip is feasible and some guests choose to make the journey. The trip costs about 180 Bs ($25) from La Paz or Santa Cruz and should last about 26 hours in the dry season.
The trip is not for the fainthearted but the landscapes are impressive. We do not recommend guests arrive by bus during the rainy season (December through March) as the road conditions can make travel impossible.
Where should I stay in Riberalta?
There are many hotel and hostels in Riberalta. Prices vary from about $50 usd a night to $8 usd. It can be difficult to make a reservations when not in Riberalta, so Pistahua’s staff can make arrangements for you. Please let us know if you would like this service and your budget.
Preparation Questions:
Do I need a Visa for Boliva?
Traveling from most countries (North & South America, Europe, Australia) you need a tourist visa; however, this can be obtained upon arrival in the airport at no cost.  We suggest visiting the website of your local embassy for more information.
Do you provide finacial assitance or scholarships?
Pisatahua designed a scholarship program to support individuals seriously committed to their healing process, who would otherwise be unable to attend a retreat. There is no discrimination in the selection process; however, special emphasis will be given to local Bolivian nationals.
For more detailed information, please refer to our ayahuasca scholarship page .
Do I need to bring extra money?
Our retreats are all inclusive and no additional funds are required once on retreat; however, guests should bring additional money for expenses occurred before and after the retreat begins. There are a few different banks with ATMs is the main plaza of Riberalta.
Guests are also welcome to leave a tip for the support staff.
What should I pack?
Please review our webpage “ What to Pack ” in the FAQ section for a detailed list of items we recommend to bring with you on retreat.
Do you provide natural soap/repellent?
We provide guests with a natural soap made from Brazil-nut oil.  We also have natural toothpaste
Guests may still want to bring their own toiletries and are welcome to do so.  Guest should make every effort possible to bring natural cosmetics, soaps/shampoos and repellents.  These natural products are not available in Riberalta, so guests must plan ahead.
What should I do about Mosquitoes?
Fortunately our center doesn’t have as many mosquitoes as many locations in the jungle. Nevertheless, mosquitoes exist and we recommend guests to bring their own natural repellents.
It is preferable to refrain from using mosquito repellent with DEET during your time with us to minimize that amount of toxic chemicals on your body and negative environmental impact. Please note that the best protection against mosquitoes is staying covered with long-sleeve shirts, pants, and socks.
*All of our buildings are well screened and secure. Every bed is also covered with a mosquito net for extra protection.
How can I best prepare for a retreat?
There are many ways to help prepare the mind and body for a retreat. We created a separate page to help answer this question in more detailed titled: How to Prepare? .
Health and Safety Questions:
Do you have COVID-19 safety measures in place?
Yes; In response to the COVID-19 virus, we’ve implemented simple, yet effective, biosecurity measures to ensure a clean, comfortable and secure environment for retreat.
Do I need to get vaccinations?
Vaccines are not required for entry into Bolivia and there is no contraindication between vaccinations and ayahuasca.  The COVID vaccine is not required to enter Bolivia.
Pisatahua is not in a position to recommend or not recommend vaccinations, so we suggest that you discuss any concerns with your doctor.
